predicted_errors.error_location: Section 2.3, definition of Bregman divergence; Lemma 2.1 and Appendix B proofs
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The displayed definition is D_R(y||p)=R(p)-R(y)-<∇R(y),p-y>, i.e. the tangent is taken at y. But Lemma 2.1, Lemma 2.2, and their proofs instead use D_R(y||p)=R(y)-R(p)-<∇R(p),y-p>, with the tangent at p. For example, the first line of the proof of Lemma 2.1 expands the divergence as R(y)-R(p)-<∇R(p),y-p>, contradicting the stated definition. The claimed proper-scoring property and minimization at p=E[y] hold for the latter orientation, not generally for the former. Thus the central calibration-to-swap-regret reduction is based on a different loss than the one formally defined.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 2.1 definition of Cal_T^D versus Lemma 2.2, Sections 3–4, and Appendices C–E
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Section 2.1 defines calibration with a 1/T factor: Cal_T^D := sum_p ((1/T) sum_t x_t(p))D(ν_p,p). However, Lemma 2.2 equates this quantity to unnormalized FullSwapReg_T, which is a sum over T rounds. Its proof obtains the unnormalized expression sum_p sum_t x_t(p)D_R(ν_p||p), with no 1/T. The later proof of Theorem 3.1, Eq. (6), labeled calibration in Appendix C, and the lower bounds all likewise use the unnormalized definition while stating bounds such as Cal_T <= εT. Under the formal Section 2.1 definition, those bounds and Lemma 2.2 are off by a factor T, and many εT claims become dimensionally/trivially inconsistent.

predicted_errors.error_location: Claim C.3 and its use in the proof of Theorem 3.1
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Claim C.3 states Cal(x)-2Cal(x̃) >= (2 diam(P)^2/H^2)T. The proof of the claim derives the opposite direction, namely Cal(x)-2Cal(x̃) <= 2T diam(P)^2/H. It therefore neither proves the stated inequality nor the inequality subsequently used in the theorem proof, which is Cal(x) <= 2Cal(x̃)+(2 diam(P)^2/H^2)T. The claimed H^{-2} error term is absent from the derivation; the displayed derivation only yields an H^{-1} term. Consequently the choices H=diam(P)/sqrt(ε) and the stated horizon bound do not follow.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 2.4 definition of Rate(P,||·||), Theorem 1.1, and simplex application in Section 1.1
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Rate(P,||·||) is defined using a regularizer whose maximum Bregman divergence max_{y,p}D_R(y||p) is finite. Yet Theorem 1.1 only assumes that the range max R-min R is at most ρ, and the simplex application asserts that negative entropy has the required rate ρ=log d. On the closed simplex, the relevant entropy Bregman divergence is KL(y||p) (under the orientation required by the later proofs), which is unbounded when p has a zero coordinate where y is positive. Bounded range of negative entropy does not imply bounded Bregman divergence; the paper itself notes this distinction immediately before Lemma 2.4. Thus negative entropy cannot establish the claimed finite Rate/simplex bound as defined, and Theorem 1.1's stated hypothesis is insufficient for the TreeSwap loss-range argument.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract versus Introduction Section 1.1 / Theorem 1.1 / Corollary C.5
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract claims simplex ℓ1 calibration after T=exp(O(log d/ε))=d^{O(1/ε)} rounds. But the abstract's preceding general statement, Theorem 1.1, the Section 1.1 simplex bullet, and Corollary C.5 all give d^{O(1/ε^2)} for nonsquared ℓ1 calibration. predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract final paragraph and lower-bound discussion in Section 1.1
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract says the lower bound proves T>=exp(Ω(1/ε)) and is tight up to constants in the exponent. The actual stated ℓ1 lower bound (Theorem 1.4 and Theorem 4.3) has only exp(Ω(min{d^{1/14},ε^{-1/6}})) or, elsewhere, a different dimension exponent. This is not an exponential-in-1/ε lower bound and cannot match either the claimed d^{O(1/ε)} abstract upper bound or the d^{O(1/ε^2)} bound stated elsewhere. The tightness conclusion is therefore unsupported and contradicts the paper's own theorem statements.

Theorem 1.4 states the horizon threshold exp(c min{d^{1/14},ε^{-1/6}}), whereas the formally stated Theorem 4.3 gives exp(c min{d^{1/7},ε^{-1/6}}). The Appendix D.1 proof applies Theorem 4.1 after a constant-factor dimension embedding and supports d^{1/14}, not d^{1/7}. Thus the stronger d^{1/7} statement in Theorem 4.3 is inconsistent with both the earlier theorem and its proof.

predicted_errors.error_location: Lemma 4.2 and proof of Theorem 4.3 in Appendix D.1
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Lemma 4.2's statement bounds swap regret using diam_{||·||}(P'), but its proof uses Hölder with ||ν_p-p|| and concludes with diam_{||·||_*}(P'). These are different quantities. In applying the lemma, the proof chooses P'=[-1,1]^{d'}, says its ℓ∞ diameter is 1 (it is 2 under the standard definition), and then claims a contradiction with Theorem 4.1. But Theorem 4.1 lower-bounds learners whose actions lie in the particular subset X⊂[-1,1]^{d'}, while the constructed learner acts over the entire cube P'; a lower bound for Δ(X) does not automatically apply to Δ(P'). Choosing P'=X could potentially repair this, but that is not the proof given.

The purported contradiction is between the constructed upper bound FullSwapReg_T <= εT and Theorem 4.1's lower bound FullSwapReg_T >= εT. These inequalities are compatible at equality, so they do not contradict each other. A constant-factor rescaling of ε might repair the argument, but it is not performed in the proof as written.
